reasons.text: Buys feedstock inside a closed loop of 3 recyclers trading the same material (39% of its feedstock)
97% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Sold products equal only 2% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed
Uploaded plant photos are near-duplicates of photos registered by 1 other plant(s)
54% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.18x the cost floor)

inspection_checklist: Trace the material flow between the plants in the loop (weighbridge slips, vehicle GPS); the same tonnes may be invoiced round a ring.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
Compare the plant against the entities sharing its identifiers (bank, address, director, photos); consider a joint inspection.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
